t:
In case of surplus reinsurance, the bordereaux is submitted ___________ as agreed between the parties.

I. Monthly
II. Quarterly
III. Yearly
e: Correct answer: I or II (from the IC85 question bank).

t: In reinsurance programme design, which of the following factor is relevant for decision making on what type of reinsurance arrangements are most suitable?
o: Management, underwriting and claims handling capab
e: Correct answer: Size and structure of portfolio (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement with regard to rate of exchange.

I. Normally the unit of currency expressed in a treaty agreement is the domestic currency of the ceding insurer concerned.
II. The treaty agreement will normally provide that the accounting and settlement will be in original currency but the domestic currencies shall form the basis of the liability of the reinsurer.
III. The ceding insurer will also retain the right in the event of major changes in the currency situation or of restrictions on currency transfers to revert partially or wholly to accounting in original currencies.
e: Correct answer: I and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t: The priority of ________, is to contain fluctuations in the insurer's results.
e: Correct answer: Direct business underwriter (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement with regard to fire proportional reinsurance business:-

I. The accounts for this type of business are normally rendered on an "Accounts Year" basis.
II. The premiums are usually shown at original gross rates and the reinsurance commission rate is then applied.
III. The reinsurance commission will cover only the ceding insurer's expenses.
e: Correct answer: I and II (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement.

I. The ultimate net loss has to exceed the net retained loss after recoveries from all other reinsurances and before the excess of loss reinsurer becomes interested.
II. Salaries of employees and office costs of the insurers are included in the calculation of the claims' costs.
III. Recoveries from proportional reinsurers, salvage, subrogation and contribution are deducted from the claims' costs.
e: Correct answer: I and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
If the reinsurance agreement includes a limitation on the reinsurer's liability during any contract period then the 'reinstatement clause' will specify:-

I. The extent of reinstatement expressed as a multiple of the per loss limit and as an amount
II. Whether the reinstatement is free or subject to an additional premium
III. Whether the reinstatement provisions apply equally to all classes of business covered by the treaty
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t: ________ is a useful tool when earnings from investment are considerably reduced due to situational changes in investment climate.
e: Correct answer: Financial reinsurance (from the IC85 question bank).

t: In Germany, the Munich Reinsurance Company was founded in ___________.
e: Correct answer: 1880 (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
On the 'losses occurring' basis method.

I. All losses occurring within the contract period are covered, no matter when the original policy was issued
II. At termination, the reinsurer is not liable for losses occurring after the contract ends, although the original policy may remain in force
III. Reinsurer at termination, remain liable for losses which occurred during the period of the contract but which had not yet been settled - whether or not the insurer is aware of these claims at the date of termination
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Which of the below factor/s have a direct effect on the results of reinsurance?

I. Efficient underwriting methods
II. Excessive generosity in the settlement of claims
III. Hasty development of business
e: Correct answer: II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement with regard to currency clause.

I. Normally the unit of currency expressed in a treaty agreement is the domestic currency of the ceding insurer concerned.
II. The treaty agreement will normally provide that the accounting and settlement will be in domestic currency and also shall form the basis of the liability of the reinsurer.
III. The ceding insurer will also retain the right in the event of major changes in the currency situation or of restrictions on currency transfers to revert partially or wholly to accounting in original currencies.
e: Correct answer: I and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Which method of calculating portfolio transfer is generally adopted under the majority of surplus and quota share treaties?

I. 50% method
II. Twenty fourth system
III. Clean cut method
e: Correct answer: Only I (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement with regard to Aggregate excess of loss reinsurance.

I. It is on the similar lines as Excess of Loss Ratio reinsurance for a defined class of business
II. It is expressed in percentages rather than amounts
III. In Aggregate Excess of loss, the amount applies as a trigger for cover instead of loss percentage / loss ratio.
e: Correct answer: I and II (from the IC85 question bank).

t: In reinsurance contract, there may also be provision for termination without notice in the event of certain other circumstances stipulated in the contract. This is known as ___________.
o: Notice of cancellation at anniversary date
e: Correct answer: Sudden death clause (from the IC85 question bank).

t: Market Terrorism Pool is an alternative carrier which operates in _____________.
e: Correct answer: India (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement with regard to Facultative Obligatory treaty.

I. This is a rare form and was in use previously.
II. This can be placed in weak reinsurance market conditions and is therefore not adequate to be relied upon for primary reinsurance capacity.
III. This form of treaty plus the high exposure / low premium market of aviation means that they are totally unbalanced.
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
In the event of insolvency of the reinurer:-

I. The Ceding insurer or cadent still has to make full payment to the insureds
II. The Ceding insurer or cadent may defer the payment to the insureds till the recovery of the amount from the reinsurer
III. The Ceding insurer or cadent has the option to default on the payment to the insureds
e: Correct answer: Only I (from the IC85 question bank).

t: In _________, premiums are held to the credit of the policyholder in an 'Experience Account'.
e: Correct answer: Finite risk programme (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
In Marine cargo reinsurance, Loss exposures fall into which of the following classes?

I. Total loss
II. General average which affect all cargo on board the vessel
III. Particular average claims which need not affect all the cargo
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

II. Accident proportional reinsurance
III. Marine proportional reinsurance

I. Fire proportional reinsurance
II. Accident proportional reinsurance
III. Marine proportional reinsurance

I. Risk inspection
II. PML assessment
III. Composite broker's intervention

In excess of loss cover, deductible is also referred as:-

I. Premium
II. Underlying
III. Priority
e: Correct answer: II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

e: Correct answer: UK (from the IC85 question bank).

Credit rating methodology used involves an examination of the:-

I. Insurer's investment portfolio
II. Investment goals
III. Asset quality
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

For fire reinsurance proportion business, premiums are usually shown:-

I. At original gross rates
II. Net of acquisition costs, agency commission, brokerage and any discount allowed to the insurer
III. Net of brokerage cost
e: Correct answer: Only I (from the IC85 question bank).

t: Which clause is usually included in a reinsurance agreement whereby it is stated that the loss to the reinsurer will not be increased due to the inability of the ceding insurer to collect from another reinsurer?
e: Correct answer: Insolvency of other reinsurers (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
What are the reasons for direct writing insurance companies to write inward reinsurance business?

I. To increase net retained premium
II. Statutory regulations
III. To achieve a lower expense ratio by the maintenance of the volume of premium income
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Treaty wordings are reinsurance agreements entered into in writing between:-

I. Insured
II. Ceding Insurer
III. Reinsurer
e: Correct answer: II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Which of the following clauses can be added under 'Commencement and termination clause'?

I. Sudden death clause
II. Notice of cancellation at anniversary date
III. Termination
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the expenditures incurred by the insurer in connection with the claim that are included in ultimate net loss.

I. Survey reports
II. Salaries of employees
III. Salvage costs
e: Correct answer: I and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t: In US, ___________ provides for an integrated approach to monitoring and analyzing the financial health of insurers and reinsurers.
e: Correct answer: IRIS (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the zones that are highly exposed to Volcanic Eruptions.

I. Japan
II. Indonesia
III. Philippines
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

Which of the following method is usually followed in most of the property proportional treaties?

I. 50% method
II. Twenty fourth system
III. Clean cut method

Identify the true statement with regard to 'reinsurance pools'.

I. Local pools are established to minimise the total reinsurance necessary outside a local market.
II. The pool operations are generally limited in scope in that they are intended to fill a specific need.
III. Normally a specialist underwriter or underwriters from one of the leading reinsurance organisations underwrite on behalf of the members participating in the pool.

II. Single Window Indian Facultative and Treaty

I. Risks emanating from the insured (technical risk)
II. Risk emanating from the insured (contractual risk)
